chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) said:
I asked him about the sacrificial animal (udhiyah) with the testicle removed, and he said, 'No.'
And whoever sacrifices a testicle-removed animal, it is incumbent upon him to repeat the sacrifice if he is able to do so. Narrated.

key_terms.اَلْأُضْحِيَّةُ: The sacrificial animal offered during Eid al-Adha

ai.seo_question: Is a sacrificial animal valid if its testicle is removed, and is repetition required?
ai.summary: In this narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies that the removal of a testicle does not constitute a defect (‘ayb) invalidating the udhiyah, distinguishing it from other disqualifying conditions. However, he mandates re-sacrificing the animal if the owner is financially capable, emphasizing the preference for completeness in worship. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor physical alterations do not nullify the ritual unless they impair the animal's utility or appearance significantly.
